trust_decision.summary: Http.read() decides where one chunked request body ends on a keep-alive HTTP/1.1 connection; at the pinned commit it skips 4 bytes after the zero-size chunk line assuming they are CRLFCRLF, so any trailer bytes stay in recv_buffer and the http1() loop parses them as the next request.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'chunked trailer'; the only chunked request-body parser is Http.read(), and its terminal-chunk branch carries the comment 'Consume CRLF, chunk size 0 and the two CRLF that follow'.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any HTTP/1.1 request with Transfer-Encoding: chunked, read through Request.receive_body for non-streaming routes (sanic/app.py:1344, sanic/request/types.py:421) or request.stream for stream=True routes
Server-side drain of an unread chunked body after the handler or error path (e.g. 405/404) in Http.http1(); the published fix also catches BadRequest here so the connection drops

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: No second chunked request parser exists: sanic/http/http3.py:212 receives body from HTTP/3 frames, sanic/asgi.py gets its body from the ASGI server, and the touchup scheme sanic/touchup/schemes/ode.py:54-79 only strips dispatch calls. The other files in the bundled LTS commits belong to separate advisories (see out_of_scope_notes).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about trailers after the zero-size chunk. A solver can argue that the unchecked chunk-data CRLF, lenient chunk-size parsing and header-name whitespace are chunk-data or header framing, not trailers, so they are out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Requests pipelined after a correctly terminated chunked body (0\r\n\r\n then GET) must still be served on the same connection. Chunk extensions on the last chunk (0;ext=1) must still parse. Clearing recv_buffer or forcing keep_alive=False after every chunked body would break pipelining.

O6_input_shapes:
trailer field after a data chunk (1
X
0
a:GET ...)
trailer after a body with only the zero-size chunk
chunk extension on the terminal chunk (0;ext=1) followed by a trailer
trailer field-name length variants that shift offsets (a: vs ab:)
fragmented delivery: zero chunk, trailer and final CRLF in separate packets
body read by a non-streaming route preload vs drained by the server after a 405/error response (the BadRequest catch in http1())
legitimate trailer such as X-Checksum: deadbeef (rejected with 400)

O7_producer.where: Framing state lives only in recv_buffer and Http.request_body (sanic/http/http1.py:278-280, sanic/http/http1.py:512); no schema, serializer, cache or config producer is involved.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The CRLF that must end each chunk's data is never checked: the next chunk-header parse skips buf[0:2] unseen and reads the size from buf[2:pos], so arbitrary bytes there are accepted (the same 'assume these bytes are CRLF' mistake the fix removes for the terminal chunk).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is chunk-data framing, not the trailer section the report names, and the fix tests all use well-formed data chunks.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same function, about 15 lines above the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: _safe_int rejects only '-', '+' and '_', so Python int(x, 16) still accepts surrounding whitespace and a 0x prefix in the chunk size. That is a size-parsing differential with front proxies on the same body-boundary decision.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Chunk-size validation has an existing hardening test (tests/test_http.py:142-167), so a solver can treat it as already handled and separate from trailers.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, helper about 80 lines below the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The header-name check compares name.lower() without rejecting whitespace before the colon, so 'Transfer-Encoding : chunked' is not seen as a body-bearing header. The body then stays in recv_buffer and is parsed as the next request.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Request-header parsing is a neighbouring feature, not chunked trailers, and the duplicate CL/TE guard at line 224 looks like the existing smuggling defence.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different method (http1_request_header), about 320 lines from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Transfer-Encoding value check that accepts a comma list ending in chunked (e.g. 'gzip, chunked') but frames it differently from the exact match.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers often widen exact-string TE checks for RFC 9112 transfer-coding lists, and the existing exact match is an obvious place to 'improve'.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An opt-in config (e.g. a REQUEST_TRAILERS flag next to KEEP_ALIVE in sanic/config.py) that parses and stores trailers into request headers, plus a second code path that skips trailer lines without validating their termination.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Trailer support is a natural feature request after trailers start being rejected outright, and it would add a config-loader route into the same body-end decision at a distance from http1.py.

O9_family: HTTP request smuggling / inconsistent message framing (CWE-444)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace 'pos += 4' with a check that the 2 bytes after the zero-size line are CRLF (or discard trailer lines up to a blank line), leaving the unchecked chunk-data CRLF and the lenient size parsing as they are.

out_of_scope_notes: The bundled LTS commits also add URITooLong for URLs over 65535 bytes (sanic/request/types.py, sanic/exceptions.py) and restrict Inspector._action to public bound methods (sanic/worker/inspector.py:88-101). These are separate advisories and are not present at the pinned commit.

Response header CRLF sanitising (sanic/response/types.py:23, 84-90, 213-215) is already present at the pinned commit (HEAD commit 'cleanup CRLF header injection'), so those hunks in the diff are no-ops here.
Most of commit 47349d68 is formatting churn (guide/, string-literal joins, nosec comments) with no security content.
